title: Cost ancestry: hierarchical cost tracing visualization & CSV export playbook
creator: Priya Natarajan
description: Design a unified Cost Ancestry view for the Redwood Console that lets users trace spend from high-level product or route down to per-request and per-token line items, visualize attribution paths, and export deterministic CSV / parquet exports for billing and chargeback. The goal is to provide a compact, scannable hierarchy (product -> route -> session/user -> request -> token groups) with rich contextual metadata (model variant, quantization, batch size, dedupe/cache hits, pricing slab) and an exportable schema that maps cleanly to billing units. This ticket captures the prototype, interaction patterns, export schema, and design decisions for PM/Eng review.
acceptance_criteria: Interactive prototype demonstrates collapse/expand of at least three hierarchy levels (product -> route -> request) with per-node cost and token counts
Hover detail panel surfaces pricing factors (model, quantization, batch, cache hit) and a link to the request trace
Export action generates a CSV schema proposal that covers node ancestry, cost breakdown, token attribution, timestamp, and pricing slab columns
Design annotated with visual treatment for negative/zero-cost credits and sampling artifacts
Accessibility review completed for color choices and keyboard navigation
Engineering review confirms feasibility for streaming export of large result sets (pagination / sampling options documented)
comments: 2025-02-10 Priya Natarajan: Kickoff - scoped goals with PM. Primary success metric is reduction in time-to-resolution for billing disputes by 40% for pilot customers. Shared initial wireframes in Figma and PRD link.

2025-02-11 Ava Chen: Uploaded first-fidelity treemap + lineage view. Two interaction patterns: nested list with inline sparklines, and force-directed ancestry graph. Requesting engineering input on scale (50k rows) and streaming export behaviour.

2025-02-12 Liam O'Connor: Engineering review - nested list is preferable for accessibility and server-side pagination. Concern: per-request token breakdown at 50k rows will need sampling or async export job. Suggested fields to include in export: request_id, parent_ids, timestamp, token_count, tokens_billed, model_variant, quantization, cost_usd, pricing_slab_id.

2025-02-13 Sofia Martinez: Data note - pricing_slab_id must be normalized to current ratecard; attach mapping table. For aggregated views, include sample_rate column to indicate sampling applied. We should include both gross_cost and net_cost columns to account for credits/discounts.

2025-02-14 Marcus Rivera (PM): Preference for single-view launch: nested list + compact ancestry breadcrumb; postpone force-graph. Add 'Export visible scope' CTA and 'Export full scope (async)' option. Add toggle for 'include token attribution' to keep export size manageable.

2025-02-15 Design critique: Accessibility flagged color contrast on negative cost chips. Iterated palette and added glyphs for cost types. Also added keyboard-first collapse/expand and focus ring states.

2025-02-16 Ava Chen: Prototype v2 uploaded with drill-in modal for request detail. Modal includes token histogram, prompt/response size, cache hit indicator, and links to raw trace. Pushed comment asking Eng to estimate async export endpoint shape.

2025-02-17 Liam O'Connor: Feasibility confirm - async export job OK; will surface job id in Console and via webhook. Estimated ENG work: 6 points. Will reuse existing batch-export infra (ENG-43210). Requires minor addition to audit log schema to record export queries (security/compliance).

2025-02-18 Marcus Rivera: Reviewed acceptance criteria. Requested one more usability round with customer success to validate chargeback column ordering and default CSV column set. Moved ticket to In Review and requested approvals from Data and Security.
2025-02-18 Elena Park (Support): Suggest adding 'example use case rows' in the UI export modal to help non-technical finance teams map fields to chargeback spreadsheets.
